subject.title: [Feature]: First-class org/team deployment — workspace scaffolding, RBAC, and deployment manifests

question: Should OpenClaw accept first-class org/team deployment as a core direction, and which pieces should become core security/config surfaces versus docs, plugins, or separate-gateway patterns?
rationale: The issue changes the documented trust model and public configuration surface; automation cannot choose the security guarantee, migration story, or product boundary safely.

options.title: Keep And Decompose
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella, then split approved work into scoped RBAC, manifest/scaffold, identity/session, and docs issues with explicit security boundaries.

options.title: Route To Existing Patterns
options.body: Decline first-class core scaffolding for now and document separate gateways, current per-agent policies, and external orchestration as the supported team-deployment path.

options.title: Narrow To RBAC Only
options.body: Move only the authorization portion to focused issues such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/49183 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87734, leaving scaffold/manifests out of core.

recommendation.title: Keep And Decompose
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella, then split approved work into scoped RBAC, manifest/scaffold, identity/session, and docs issues with explicit security boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest observed history across the current trust-boundary docs and agent CLI surface involved in the product/security decision.
